title: Book a medical check-up by chasing hospitals over email
summary: A poster's AI agent emailed hospitals, kept following up and moved on when one went quiet; they say the check-up was booked without ever talking to the hospital.
agent_role: The agent sent the booking emails, followed up, and decided when to drop an unresponsive hospital for the next one. The poster only turned up for the appointment.
outcome: The author reports the check-up was booked without speaking to the hospital once before walking in.
what_they_did: The poster had an AI agent book a medical check-up by email. The agent kept following up with the hospital. If one went quiet while time was tight, it switched to the next option.
how_it_went: The author says the booking was confirmed. They never spoke to the hospital until they walked in.
worth_knowing: The author argues the real value is in the follow-ups, not the first request. This matters most where replies are slow, as they find in Southeast Asia.
prompt: Help me book a [type of appointment] at a clinic or hospital in [your city] between [date range]. List 3-5 suitable providers and draft a booking request email for each. Show me the drafts and wait for my approval before sending anything. After that, check my email daily for replies and draft polite follow-ups if there is no answer within [number] days. If one goes quiet and time is short, suggest moving to the next provider. Ask me before confirming any booking.

curation.rationale: A genuine multi-step health-admin task: the agent emailed, chased replies and switched hospitals when one went quiet. Evidence is thin and the platform is unnamed, but it is a useful non-coding pattern.
